clue.text: Plenty of effective anaesthetic?

definitions.meaning: a ... of things means plenty of them, a sizeable quantity
read whimsically, something that numbs well would be a ..., a fine numbing agent

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the last word as numb + er, a thing that numbs, which is why the question mark is there.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a good number of' means a fair quantity, so it can stand for plenty.

clue.text: Remake of "I Claudius" turn off? I'm wanting to end it all

definitions.text: I'm wanting to end it all

indicators.note: a remake of a film is a reworking, so the letters of the title are rearranged
off says a piece is taken away from the title's letters before they are reworked

parts.note: a U-turn gives U for turn

explanation.surface: A film buff grumbles that yet another remake of the Roman drama I, Claudius makes them despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes one U from I CLAUDIUS, leaving ICLADIUS, and 'Remake of' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wanting to end it all has a wish for death, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Retranslation, perhaps, of author of 16

definitions.meaning: split as R.E. translation: the Royal Engineers' word for one of their soldiers, i.e. what a member of the RE is called
the pen name of H. C. McNeile, who wrote the thriller hero at 16

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Retranslation' as 'RE translation': in the British Army a private of the Royal Engineers (RE) is known by this title.
explanation.definitionFit: H. C. McNeile wrote the Bulldog Drummond novels under this pseudonym, taken from his Royal Engineers service.

clue.text: Take scenic route with blower?

definitions.meaning: to meander or follow a twisting path, as a scenic road does
something that blows, i.e. moving air or a breeze

explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to twist and turn along a way; wind is also the air that blows.

clue.text: Deprived of primary carer when crook mounted her

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or out of order, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A child lost their mother when some villain climbed up on top of her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a villain in the story, but here it signals that MOUNTEDHER is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is the usual primary carer, so a child lacking one has been deprived of her.

clue.text: So much for the French — a shapeless unfinished piece of metal

parts.note: French 'tant' means so much, as in 'tant pis'

indicators.note: unfinished says the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a lump is a shapeless mass, so a shapeless piece is a lump

explanation.surface: Dismissing French contributions, a sculptor grumbles about an unfinished lump of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the final P of A LUMP, giving ALUM; 'piece of' just joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantalum is a hard blue-grey metallic element used in electronics.

clue.text: Means of fighting an order in London

indicators.note: in says the order goes inside the word for London

parts.note: William Cobbett called London 'the Great Wen', a wen being a swelling
a PO is a postal order, so an order gives A plus PO

explanation.surface: A soldier asks where in the capital a military order might be carried out.
explanation.walkthrough: A postal order is a British money transfer bought at a post office; WEN for London is an old crossword favourite from Cobbett's 'Great Wen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A weapon is any instrument used in combat, so it is a means of fighting.

clue.text: Every 22 across 21 across has broken 3 like us

parts.note: every compass point gives the four letters N, E, W and S

indicators.note: broken says the letters of that answer are smashed into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 3 down, the author's pen name

explanation.surface: A grumble that every direction finds the soldier at 3 down broken, just like us.
explanation.walkthrough: The four cardinal points give their initials; 'broken' rearranges the six letters of the answer at 3 down. 'Us' is the Guardian speaking, a daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle appeared in the Guardian, so things like us are daily publications of news.

clue.text: Turn left amid cheers for release

indicators.note: amid says the turn and left go into the middle of the cheers

parts.note: an ovation is a round of cheers
a U-turn gives U for turn

explanation.surface: A driver is told to turn left in the middle of a cheering crowd to get free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'release' looks like a getaway in the surface, but it is the definition in its biological sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovulation is the release of an egg from the ovary.

clue.text: A beleaguered part of Poplar

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A besieged corner of the East London district of Poplar.
explanation.walkthrough: Poplar is also a district of East London, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar tree, Populus alba.

clue.text: Crab takes a month on a case …

parts.note: DEC is the abbreviation for December
a pod is a seed case, so a case gives A plus POD

explanation.surface: A crab spends a month in its shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'on' are link words putting the month before A POD.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs belong to the decapods, the ten-legged crustaceans, so a crab is an example.

clue.text: … earlier piece more like squid

parts.note: following on from the previous clue's December, the month earlier is October, abbreviated OCT
an opus is a piece of music or writing

explanation.surface: Continuing the seafood: an earlier creature is closer to a squid than the crab.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the clue before: its month was December, so the 'earlier' month here is October.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are cephalopods with arms, so an octopus resembles a squid much more than a crab does.

clue.text: A French theologian keeping ceremonial robes attacked by 3

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: keeping says the theologian holds the robes inside

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
ermine is the white fur trimming worn on ceremonial robes, by peers or judges

explanation.surface: A French divine in ceremonial robes is set upon by the soldier at 3 down.
explanation.walkthrough: A sapper (3 down) digs tunnels under enemy walls, so what he attacks is literally dug from beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappers dig under fortifications, so something attacked by one has been dug away from below.

clue.text: Old has-been, devoid of energy, playing "My Fair Lady"?

indicators.note: playing a part means taking on a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: devoid of says one letter is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A washed-up old actor, out of energy, is playing in the musical My Fair Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoid of' removes one E from HAS-BEEN, leaving HASBEN; with OLD, 'playing' rearranges those nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair-haired woman could be called 'my fair lady', and this pale shade of hair is one such fairness.

clue.text: A great grand rumpus (ending so soon, one rather suspects) — we started it

definitions.text: A great grand rumpus (ending so soon, one rather suspects) — we started it

indicators.note: the word starts of the clue are what count, so the opening letter of each word up to this point is taken

explanation.surface: Those who began a huge brawl that fizzled out quickly confess it was their doing.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the first ten words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes such people.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressors are the side that starts a fight, the ones who would admit 'we started it'.

clue.text: Conclusion to different setter's warmth of heart?

parts.note: a conclusion is an end
other means different
the setter's own possession is 'my'

explanation.surface: A different crossword setter shows warmth of heart at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warmth of heart' reads as kindliness, but the question mark points to heat made from within, as in warm-blooded animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Endothermy is an animal's generation of its own body heat internally, a literal warmth within.

clue.text: Thriller hero gets clip on ear (part of), day not finished

parts.note: a bulldog clip is a sprung metal clip for papers
the eardrum is part of the ear

indicators.note: not finished says the end of the day's name is cut off

parts.note: Monday is a day of the week

explanation.surface: A thriller's hero gets clipped round the ear on a day of unfinished business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' drops the AY of MONDAY to leave MOND. 'gets' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulldog Drummond is the gentleman adventurer of Sapper's 1920s thrillers.

clue.text: Yellow streak will put celebrity status out of order in time

indicators.note: in says the shortened status goes inside the time

parts.note: a day is a period of time

indicators.note: out of says the order is taken away from the celebrity status

parts.note: stardom is the status of a celebrity
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A coward's streak will knock fame out of order in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' tempts as an anagram signal, but here 'out of' is a removal and 'order' is a British honour; 'in' puts what is left inside the time. 'will put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow streak is a vein of cowardice, and dastardy is cowardly meanness.

clue.text: Paladin docked with his top half mashed in cooker

indicators.note: docked says the tail letter is cut off, as a dog's tail is docked

parts.note: Oliver was one of the twelve Paladins of Charlemagne

indicators.note: mashed says those letters are crushed into a new order
top half keeps only the first half of the name, the rest removed

parts.note: his refers back to the paladin, so it stands for his name again

explanation.surface: A knight with his tail cut off has the top half of him mashed in a cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top half' keeps OLI of OLIVER and 'mashed' rearranges it. The definition is loose: something you cook in.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive oil is a cooking medium, something food is fried or cooked in.

clue.text: Greek island boy reported at offshore anchorage

indicators.note: reported says the words are spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island and Ted a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad from a Greek island is said to be at an offshore mooring.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, the island and the boy's name give a word for a sheltered stretch of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadstead is a stretch of sheltered water near the shore where ships can lie at anchor.

clue.text: Fish that's died after head removed to make marzipan

indicators.note: after says the D comes behind the beheaded fish
head removed says the first letter is cut off

parts.note: salmon is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish has died after being beheaded to make a sweet paste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head removed' cuts the first letter from the fish, and 'after' places the abbreviation for died behind it; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Marzipan is made from ground almonds and sugar, so the nut is what you use to make it.

clue.text: See 22
See 8
Cardinal of the Rose to go round on the spot

parts.note: to compass is to go round or encircle
a point is a spot or place

explanation.surface: A cardinal of a rose-adorned church must go round on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' tempts as a churchman; it is one of the four cardinal points on a compass rose, the star-shaped dial on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: North, east, south and west are the cardinal points, the main markings of the compass rose.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation for hammers?

definitions.meaning: a site of tents or huts for a short stay
hammy actors overact in an exaggerated, affected style

explanation.walkthrough: Hammers are hams, overacting performers; theatrically affected behaviour is this. 'for' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A site of tents is short-term shelter; overacted, affected performance is described as camp too.

clue.text: Drink with army branch, the greatest

parts.note: to sup is to drink
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Having a drink with an army unit is the best thing there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link putting the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in rank or quality, the greatest of all.

clue.text: Peter is reliable

definitions.meaning: in criminal slang a peter is a strongbox
trustworthy and secure, not to be feared

explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a man's name, but in old thieves' slang it is a strongbox for valuables. 'is' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox is called this, and a reliable pair of hands is also said to be this.

clue.text: See 13
Movement for change: simmer mixture for entering

indicators.note: entering says the second for goes inside the reworked letters
a mixture is a stirring together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe step: simmer the mixture before adding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' (as in stir the mixture) rearranges REMISM from the six cooking letters, and 'entering' sends the second 'for' into them; the first 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Reformism is a political movement seeking gradual change rather than revolution.
